title: Nvidia Just Gave Away the Next Boom (THIS IS HUGE!)
creator: BWB - Business With Brian
summary: Brian frames AI as a brain and its reflexes: Nvidia now reports data center (the brain) separately from edge computing (the reflexes in PCs, cars and robots), and he argues both win because every device reflex sends more work back to the brain — with the brain growing about four times faster today and the reflexes set to become the bigger business in the early to mid-2030s. After mid-October's chip sell-off (the longest losing streak since 2008, about $2 trillion gone), his signal ladder puts Nvidia at severely undervalued at about 23 times next year's earnings, with data-center revenue of about $89 billion in a quarter; he dollar-cost averages down. Broadcom is undervalued (slightly undervalued after risk adjustment, given its up-to-$71 billion financing for one customer). Micron is off his ladder for lack of a trusted valuation, SanDisk sits in his reassess-the-business tier, Qualcomm and ARM are slightly overvalued to fairly valued at about 100 times earnings, Ambarella is fairly valued pending a growth re-acceleration, Tesla is fairly valued on outside estimates, Alphabet is fairly valued with good news priced in, and Amazon is slightly undervalued but he wants this week's earnings first. A sponsored Greenland Mines segment is not recorded as a call. Calls: NVDA and AVGO — BUY; AMZN and AMBA — CONDITIONAL_BUY; GOOGL — HOLD, flipped from BUY; TSLA — HOLD; MU, SNDK, QCOM and ARM — UNCERTAIN.

calls.price_at_call: about 23x next year's earnings (stated); no share price stated
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY; no flip) — his signal ladder puts Nvidia right on the line for 'severely undervalued', the deepest undervalued tier, and his risk-adjusted system lands in the same place; his method is to dollar-cost average on the way down. The mid-October chip sell-off (longest losing streak since 2008, about $2trn wiped) is in his view a phenomenal buying opportunity.
calls.base_case: Data center revenue about $89bn in a single quarter, more than double a year earlier, while edge computing grew about 27% and is only about 7.5% of sales; Amazon, Google and Meta alone plan roughly $550bn of 2026 spending and none has cut since the sell-off.
calls.bull_case: Every edge device sends more work back to the data center, so both sides win; Nvidia guides AI infrastructure toward $3-4trn a year by the end of the decade and Dell'Oro sees data-center spending passing $3trn a year by 2030, with memory supply locked via about $279bn of supplier commitments.
calls.bear_case: Memory costs squeeze gross margin to about 71-72 cents per dollar from 75, and UBS expects big-cloud spending growth to slow sharply by 2028 — he thinks that is too soon, but it is the consensus bear case.

calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY; no flip) — Broadcom sits at 'undervalued' on his ladder; his risk-adjusted system pulls it back to 'slightly undervalued' only because of financing uncertainty, not the business.
calls.base_case: Custom AI chips co-designed one customer at a time (Google, Meta, Anthropic among them); AI chip sales about $17bn in a single quarter, more than three times a year earlier, with inference productisation strengthening.
calls.bull_case: As edge requests outgrow devices they route to data centers where Broadcom-designed chips answer them, so Broadcom gets paid on the round trip alongside Nvidia.
calls.bear_case: Customers cannot always pay upfront: Broadcom has agreed to back or lend up to $71bn to just one customer (Reuters reports it is believed to be Anthropic); whales are neutral and insiders, including a co-founder on a set plan, have been selling.

calls.thesis: CONDITIONAL_BUY (was BUY; buy-side stance kept, no flip flagged) — his system just moved Amazon to 'slightly undervalued', but it reports this coming week and he says he really wants to see those numbers before he takes action.
calls.base_case: AWS has about $496bn of signed contracts still to deliver, more than double nine months ago; Alexa is given away with Prime and people who try it sign up for Prime at nearly 25% higher rates.
calls.bull_case: Amazon owns both an edge surface (Alexa/devices) and the cloud the work routes to, so it collects the toll at both ends of the round trip.
calls.bear_case: Big money is split — some funds added while one named fund cut about a quarter of its stake — so he reads no clear institutional signal ahead of the print.

calls.stance_flip: BWB was BUY on GOOGL (last tracked BUY, 2025 'toll collector' video), now HOLD — his system has Alphabet at 'fairly valued' and he says most of its good news is already in the price.
calls.thesis: HOLD — FLIP from BUY: Alphabet is his first 'toll collector' (paid at both the data-center and edge ends), but at fairly valued he is not adding here.
calls.base_case: Google Cloud grew about 82% and its backlog more than tripled to about $514bn in three quarters; Apple will build its next AI models, including the new Siri, on Gemini, so Alphabet gets paid every time an iPhone thinks; AI subscriptions run from about $5 to about $200 a month.
calls.bull_case: Whales are 'leaning in quietly', and the toll-collector position pays whichever side of the brain/reflex split grows faster.
calls.bear_case: Alphabet is spending cash faster than it comes in and is selling stock to cover the gap, which caps the near-term value case.

calls.price_at_call: about 200x next year's earnings (stated); no share price stated
calls.thesis: HOLD, first tracked BWB TSLA call (no flip) — his ladder has Tesla at 'fairly valued', but the reading rests only on outside estimates, and he takes Elon Musk's claims at about 10% of face value.
calls.base_case: About 1.7 million people pay for Full Self-Driving and for the first time half are on the $99-a-month plan — the one edge asset already collecting monthly revenue; latest-quarter spending on factories and computing roughly doubled year over year.
calls.bull_case: If humanoid robots and robotaxis scale even on the realistic path (Goldman Sachs: about 1m robotaxis worldwide by 2030, 6m by 2035; Bank of America: about 1.2m humanoids a year by 2030), Tesla is betting hardest on the winning category.
calls.bear_case: Musk's goal of 10 million robots a year is over eight times Bank of America's whole-market 2030 forecast; only about 25,000 humanoids shipped worldwide in the first half of 2026 and about 740 robotaxis were registered in Texas by mid-October versus the 1m promised for 2020; whales have been leaving for three quarters.

calls.thesis: CONDITIONAL_BUY reiterated (was CONDITIONAL_BUY on his watch list; no flip) — Ambarella (auto-captions render 'Amberella') is his pure edge play, but his system has it only 'fairly valued' on analyst-based readings he does not weight heavily, and he wants growth to tick back up before he really gets interested.
calls.base_case: Its chips sit behind camera lenses in security cameras, car cameras, drones and warehouse robots, deciding what the camera looks at on-device without sending video to the cloud.
calls.bull_case: If edge AI adoption inflects, a pure-play on-device vision name re-rates, and about 14% of shares being sold short leaves room for a squeeze on better growth.
calls.bear_case: Growth has slowed for six quarters in a row to about 13%, and the big funds have been heading for the exits.
